description: flatten-single incorrectly unwraps the modules list when it contains exactly one entry. This causes manifest-modules to return the module entry itself (a list of fields) instead of a list of entries, leading to incorrect iteration and failure to index the module in manifest->module-index.
suggested_fix: Do not use flatten-single for the 'modules' field in parse-manifest. The 'modules' field is naturally a list of entries (which are themselves lists), and flatten-single's heuristic for unwrapping single-element lists is inappropriate here.

description: parse-module-entry strictly requires the 'subdir' tag to be the first element in a nested module entry list. If 'subdir' appears after other fields (like 'description'), the entry will not be recognized, leading to missing modules in the index.
suggested_fix: Refactor the detection of nested module entries to use (assq 'subdir mod) or a similar order-independent check.

description: module-index-build! clears the global index hashtables at the start of the build process. Because these hashtables are likely already injected into the core module system, any concurrent lookups during the build (which involves disk I/O) will return empty or incomplete results.
suggested_fix: Build the index in fresh hashtables and then swap them into the global variables and re-inject them into the core system to ensure the update is atomic and the system remains functional during indexing.

description: module-index-lookup assumes any module name containing a slash is a namespaced name (skill/module). However, modules in subdirectories also have slashes in their names (e.g., 'util/vec'). The current logic prevents these from being found in the simple index even if they are unique and the user provides the correct relative path.
code_snippet:
(if (module-index-string-contains? name-str "/")
           ;; Namespaced: check namespaced index only
           (hashtable-ref *manifest-namespaced-idx* name #f)
suggested_fix: Update lookup logic to check the simple index even if a slash is present, or specifically check if the prefix before the first slash corresponds to a known skill name before deciding it is a namespaced lookup.

description: find-manifests uses directory-list without sorting. This makes the order of manifest discovery dependent on filesystem ordering, which makes the 'first-win' collision resolution logic in module-index-build! non-deterministic.
suggested_fix: Sort the results of directory-list to ensure a stable and deterministic discovery order across different environments.

description: The fallback to *manifest-namespaced-idx* for simple names (those without slashes) is ineffective because the namespaced index keys are constructed using a slash separator, making them unreachable via simple name lookup.
suggested_fix: Remove the redundant lookup or implement a mechanism to resolve ambiguous simple names by searching for matching suffixes in the namespaced index.
